text: 🔥🇲🇽 Every federal contract, published monthly. Pemex and CFE subsidiaries open their books. "Right now it's published every three months. We're going to publish monthly — every contract of the Federal Government will be published every month." — Raquel Buenrostro, Anticorruption Secretary The decree hits four areas: public contracting, Pemex/CFE subsidiaries (financial statements, corporate governance, reports filed with foreign agencies), audits, and an open invitation to all branches and levels of government. The 17 old reserve categories collapse into two: public interest and national security.

🇲🇽⚖️ "It is total transparency of the Government of Mexico." "With this Decree we no longer leave it 'to the criterion of the public servant'... It is total transparency of the Government of Mexico." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, signing the transparency decree Signed this morning: no official — not a secretary, not a Pemex or CFE director — decides alone what stays classified. Only national security and open proceedings can be reserved, and even then in public versions. The old INAI cost over a billion pesos a year — and its portal "was down all the time." The decree goes to Congress in September to become law.

🇲🇽🌾 26,800 corn growers. 348,000 hectares. 4,566 million pesos — delivered today. "26,800 corn producers are receiving these incentives — covering 3.5 million tonnes across 348,045 hectares. The total: 4,566 million pesos." — Columba Jazmín López, Agriculture Secretary, live from Culiacán With international corn prices at historic lows, Mexico struck a production deal with ~100,000 growers, seed and fertilizer suppliers, and the big flour mills. Today the first Bienestar cards were handed out in Sinaloa — the country's #1 white corn producer. Registration stays open until August 15.

🇲🇽🚢 <u>MEXICO'S EXPORTS TO THE US JUST HAD THEIR BEST JUNE EVER</u>

Tariff noise or not, Mexico shipped 55,254 million dollars in goods to the United States in June — the best June in history, El Financiero reports. First-half exports reached 298,157 million, keeping Mexico the top supplier of the US economy while China slid to fifth place. And the street runs both ways: Mexico was also the number-one destination for US exports, taking 33,912 million in June, up 22%.

🇲🇽🛡️ <u>INEGI CONFIRMS HISTORIC HOMICIDE DROP: RATE DOWN TO 21.4</u>

Mexico closed 2025 with 27,989 homicides — 18% fewer than the 33,550 recorded in 2024 — and a rate of 21.4 per 100,000 people, down from 25.6, INEGI's death-certificate statistics confirm. Under Sheinbaum's National Security Strategy, intentional homicides have fallen 48% between September 2024 and June 2026. The "failed state" narrative just lost another round to the data.

🇲🇽📵 <u>HAIDT AT THE MAÑANERA: BAN PHONES IN MEXICO'S SCHOOLS</u>

Psychologist Jonathan Haidt brought the evidence straight to President Sheinbaum's morning press conference: a phone-based childhood "causes depression, anxiety, eating disorders, addiction, distraction" — and the tech giants knew, then "lied about it." His two asks for Mexico: smartphones banned for the entire school day and a minimum age of 16 for social media. "I encourage you, President Sheinbaum, to implement both measures in Mexico." The government's consultation with parents and teachers is already underway — school rules land at the end of this month.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>BEANY LOZANO'S SUSPECTED KILLER CAUGHT IN SINALOA</u>

Federal forces arrested José Manuel Rubio Santini, "El Tito," in Guasave, Sinaloa — accused of shooting his partner, UNACH student Beany Lozano García, in Tuxtla Chico, Chiapas, last April and leaving her wounded inside a truck for five hours; she died eleven days later. The capture came from joint intelligence work by the SSPC, the FGR, Sedena and the National Intelligence Center, with a 500,000-peso reward on his head. He crossed half the country to hide. It didn't save him.

🇲🇽🎓 <u>UNAM RESETS: IN-PERSON EXAM FOR 58,000 ASPIRANTS, CLASSES AUG 31</u>

After the AI-tainted online admissions fiasco, UNAM publishes today the dates and venues for an in-person control exam covering 58,000 aspirants flagged with anomalous perfect scores. New-entry classes are pushed to August 31, in line with the SEP calendar, rector Leonardo Lomelí announced. Nobody keeps a tainted score, nobody loses their place without a fair shot. That's what a public university does.

🇲🇽📊 <u>MEXICAN CONSUMERS SHAKE OFF THE GLOOM: CONFIDENCE UP IN JULY</u>

Mexico's consumer confidence index rose 1.1 points in July to 45 points, INEGI reports — households are moderating their pessimism while the usual voices insist the economy is falling apart. La Jornada notes families judge their own finances clearly better than the country's. The people living the economy trust it more than the people writing about it.

‍IPI: Mexico: IPI raises alarm as violence against journalists escalates August 3, 2026 | 🟢 📰 The International Press Institute documents seven journalists killed in Mexico in 2026 — one under state protection, four municipal police arrested in the Roxana Guzmán case, threats reported before most of the killings. Veracruz is the epicenter. No caricature: names, dates, case status, and direct requests to five state attorneys general. The demand is accountability, not intervention. • "one of the journalists killed this year was under state protection" • "seven Mexican journalists in the first seven months of 2026"
